title: Locale's Banned Ingredients
summary: The full list of ingredients Locale does not use, including potassium sorbate and calcium propionate, and the reasoning behind each exclusion.
body_markdown:
At Locale, we have put hundreds of hours into researching the ingredients that go into our meals, making sure that everything we put into our food was optimized for your performance today and health tomorrow.


Over time, we developed a list of banned ingredients, or ingredients that we would never use in our food. This list is expanded over time with the most up to date research on health and nutrition.


The list currently runs to more than 60 ingredients and practices. It is applied to every meal on the menu, and it is the reason some otherwise-popular ingredients never appear.


Last updated: August 2026

## Frequently asked questions


How many ingredients does Locale ban?


More than 60 ingredients and practices, grouped into nine categories covering sweeteners, colours, flavour enhancers, preservatives, processed fats, additives and farming practices.


Why are seed oils on the banned list?


Locale cooks with olive and avocado oil only. Seed oils are excluded across the whole menu, including in sauces and dressings, where they most often appear unnoticed.


Does Locale ban all sugar, or only refined sugar?


The banned list covers refined sugars and artificial sweeteners — refined white, cane and beet sugar, high fructose corn syrup, sucralose, aspartame and sugar alcohols among them.


Are the meals tested, or is the banned list self-declared?


Both. The list governs what goes in, and ingredients are third-party lab tested by Light Labs for heavy metals, pesticides, phthalates and PFAS, with the results published.


How often does the banned list change?


It is expanded over time as research develops. The date it was last updated is shown at the top of this page.
